analysis:
Reviewed the supplied BASE text of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 1-818). The PR change is documentation only: head lines 1717-1843 add a 'Native Flint' section describing the model_type flint adapter, FlintModel.cbv2Prefill (omitting vocab projection for evaluation-only chunks), and a strict model-owned loader. The patch excerpt is truncated and no head-side text was supplied, so I could not verify the remainder of the new section. No executable code, configuration, or controls changed in what I saw, so I found no concrete security regression.

Threat-model areas touched by the doc: TB-007 (inference engine), A-004/T-012/T-027 (model weights and checkpoint integrity), and T-041 (prefix cache). The visible text says the strict loader rejects missing, extra, or duplicate tensors and conflicting aliases. That is consistent with the weight-integrity posture and does not claim a weight-hash or attestation guarantee. I did not see any statement weakening the prefix-cache scope, TTL, or SSD-tier guarantees in T-041.

Open integration questions: (1) the new Flint adapter is production code in other files. How it handles prefix-cache and cacheSalt scoping, SSD donation gating, and the weight-hash verification path is outside this batch. (2) The `cbv2Prefill` path that skips the vocab projection for evaluation-only chunks should be checked against prefix-cache checkpoint and receipt correctness. (3) Whether `flint` appears in the advertised-model and weight-hash registries cannot be determined from the supplied text. Source code for these items is not in scope here, so this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
